problem: Investors questioned the business, governance and losses.
title: WeWork's parent pulls its IPO after investors balk at its valuation
context: SoftBank had invested at a $47 billion valuation in January 2019, and the company filed to go public.
decision_made: Withdraw the IPO filing on 30 September 2019, a week after Adam Neumann gave up the CEO role.
action_taken: Two co-CEOs said they would focus on the core business; the company planned layoffs and sales of acquired businesses.
observed_outcome: The IPO did not happen. Reports said the target valuation had fallen to well below $20 billion and a $6 billion bank loan deal hinged on a successful share sale. SoftBank was to provide $1.5 billion the following year.
lessons: A valuation set by private investors may not survive public market scrutiny of governance and losses.
limitations: No formal rescue package was described in the sources used. Later events were not checked.

claims.claim_text: WeWork's parent withdrew its IPO filing on 30 September 2019, about a week after Neumann stepped down as CEO.
A $6 billion bank loan deal depended on a successful share sale of at least $3 billion.
